prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-03-19. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.34 |
| Retained earnings       | 22,804M |
| Current liabilities     | 20,957M |
| Current assets          | 28,007M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 31,211M |
| Total liabilities       | 34,289M |
| Total assets            | 67,064M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,494M |
| Revenue                 | 18,044M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-03-19, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company exhibits a decent current ratio (1.34) and substantial retained earnings, suggesting good liquidity and financial stability. However, the high total liabilities relative to total assets (around 51% debt financing) and the modest EBIT margin (13.82%) indicate a leveraged position and somewhat constrained profitability that might limit its ability to absorb financial shocks.
DECISION: BBB-
